I am old now, 85 years, and my strength is not what it was. This small plot of mine in Mwanza, just over a third of a hectare, I plant with cassava mixed with some sweet potato and beans — they do not need much from me, and cassava will not fail me even if the rains are poor. I cannot afford the chemical fertilizer from the shop, but I put the manure from my few chickens and goats on the soil, and my grandchildren help me with the digging and weeding when they come from school. We have no pump or canal here, so I wait for the rains like everyone else.
